quickAnswer: Concord has an unusually high vacancy rate (6.2%, 5th of 50 towns) and a median home value of $1,018,100 (6th of 50). Its electric utility is a municipal light plant, so the heat pump rebate path depends on how the house is heated.
body: ## Empty houses still have boilers

In the 2022 American Community Survey (ACS), Concord shows 6,863 housing units, and 424 of them stood vacant, a vacancy rate of 6.2%. That is the 5th-highest rate among the 50 towns we serve, against 3.6% for the middle town. A vacant house can still have a furnace or boiler, and a home that sits empty through winter generally needs its heat held at a safe minimum and its equipment looked over before the cold arrives.
## What the median Concord home is worth

The median owner-occupied home in Concord is valued at $1,018,100 (ACS 2022), the 6th-highest among the 50 towns and far above the $579,150 of the middle town. Whatever a house is worth, the work is the same: size the equipment to the building and get a written estimate before anything starts. A house at that value still gets measured first, and a unit chosen to last for decades should be sized to the numbers rather than to the old nameplate.
## Gas leads, oil is still a big second

Utility gas heats 55.1% of occupied Concord homes and fuel oil heats 27.9%. Electricity accounts for 9.1% and bottled or tank gas for 4.7%. With more than a quarter of homes on oil, an oil home's replacement choice can run between a new oil boiler, a gas conversion where a main is available, and a heat pump. A gas home has a simpler question: replace like for like, or add a heat pump alongside. Electricity and bottled gas serve smaller groups, and for an electric-resistance or propane house a heat pump is often worth pricing. Venting, piping and the permit all depend on the fuel and the equipment chosen.
## A town founded in 1635

Concord was established in 1635 by English settlers, the first inland colonial settlement in New England. The land, situated at the confluence of the Sudbury and Assabet rivers, was known as Musketaquid, an Algonquian word for grassy plain, a name that fits the low-lying marshes and kettle holes. The battles of Lexington and Concord began on April 19, 1775, and in the 19th century the town became home to Emerson, Hawthorne, Alcott and Thoreau. Two of their houses on Lexington Road, The Wayside and Orchard House, are museums today.

In the ACS, 21.8% of Concord's housing units date from 1939 or earlier, the 10th-highest share of the 50 towns, and the median home was built in 1967. About two thirds of the units are single-family detached houses, and multi-unit buildings make up 28.4% of the total, the 12th-highest share of the 50 towns. In general, old and mid-century houses, apartment buildings and newer construction call for different sizing and different ductwork or piping, so the load assessment comes before the quote.
## A municipal light plant, and the rebate question

The Concord Municipal Light Plant, a municipal utility, supplies the electricity here, and that decides which heat pump program to chase. The Mass Save whole-home rebate is aimed mainly at gas-heated houses in a municipal territory. An oil, propane or electric house would start with the light plant's own program instead, and we do not quote what it pays. Our [heat pump page](/cities/concord/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) lays out the 2026 numbers.

faq.q: Can I get a Mass Save heat pump rebate in Concord?
faq.a: Possibly, depending on how the house heats. The light plant serving Concord is municipal, so the Mass Save route is mostly open to gas-heated homes and everyone else checks the light plant's own program first. Programs change, so confirm both before you buy equipment.

faq.q: My Concord house heats with oil. Is it time to consider a heat pump?
faq.a: It may be, especially when the oil boiler is old or the repair bills are mounting. Oil heats 27.9% of Concord homes (ACS 2022). A heat pump can supply both heating and cooling, but whether it can carry the whole house depends on insulation and sizing. We assess the heating load first, then give a written estimate.

faq.q: What should I do about heat in a Concord house that will sit empty?
faq.a: Usually it is better to keep the heat on at a safe minimum than to shut the system off, and have the equipment serviced before the cold season. The ACS 2022 counts 6.2% of Concord's housing units as vacant. If you are unsure what setting is safe for your house, ask us.

faq.q: Does the age of my Concord house change what I should install?
faq.a: It can. Concord has 1,498 units from 1939 or earlier and 1,379 from 2000 or later (ACS 2022), and the two groups call for different sizing, piping and insulation checks. Measuring the load for your own house is the reliable way to decide, whatever its year.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Gas heats 3,545 occupied Concord homes (55.1%) and oil heats 1,794 (27.9%), so most replacement jobs start as a choice between a like-for-like swap and a change of fuel. The median home dates to 1967.
body: ## Two big fuel groups

The ACS 2022 counts 3,545 occupied homes on utility gas and 1,794 on fuel oil. Concord ranks 16th of the 50 towns for gas and 32nd for oil. For a gas customer, the usual job is a same-fuel swap. An oil customer has a wider menu: another oil boiler, a gas line where one can reach the house, or a heat pump.
## Age of the house

A median build year of 1967 puts many units in the middle bands: 1,721 date from 1960 to 1979 and 1,278 from 1940 to 1959. At the old end, 1,498 units (21.8%) go back to 1939 or earlier. A boiler or furnace chosen decades ago was matched to the house as it stood then, so we measure today's heat loss before pricing a new one instead of copying the old nameplate.
## The smaller fuel groups

Electricity heats 583 homes (9.1%) and bottled gas heats 302 (4.7%). Wood serves 34, another 129 homes use other fuels or coal, and 52 report none. An electric-resistance house is a natural candidate for the [heat pump option](/cities/concord/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits). A propane house can compare its tank fuel against a gas or electric alternative.
## Permit and inspection

A gas furnace or boiler swap is a permitted job. A licensed plumber or gas fitter has to pull the permit, and an inspection closes it out. The town's building department can say what a particular job needs.
## Tenants and landlords

Concord counts 1,576 renter households (24.5%), so a good share of boilers here are run by someone other than the person who lives with them. The State Sanitary Code sets minimums of 68 F by day and 64 F overnight in the heating season (105 CMR 410.201), and heat is the landlord's cost unless the lease says otherwise. That is general information, not legal advice.
## When the heat stops

Breakdowns do not keep office hours. Call (508) 786-8755 and emergency calls are taken around the clock, with a free written estimate before any work begins. The wider picture of the town is on the [Concord overview](/cities/concord).

faq.q: How do I decide between repairing and replacing a Concord boiler?
faq.a: A single failed part on a fairly young unit is usually worth repairing. Repeated faults on an old unit, or a safety defect found on inspection, point toward replacement. We look at the unit and the house, then price both routes in writing before work starts.

faq.q: Can a Concord oil house switch to gas?
faq.a: Only where gas service reaches the property. Utility gas heats 3,545 Concord homes, but whether a line runs to your street is a question for the gas company, and we can raise it during the estimate. A heat pump is the other alternative worth pricing.

faq.q: What if my Concord home is heated with electricity?
faq.a: Electric heat serves 583 homes in town (ACS 2022). Resistance heat is often a good candidate for a heat pump, which does both heating and cooling. Insulation and the size of the load decide how much of the house one can carry.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Concord has 4,557 single-family detached houses and 1,515 homes in buildings of five or more units. Those two types need different cooling plans, and many older homes were built without central air, so ductless is often an option.
body: ## Cooling a detached house versus an apartment

The ACS 2022 counts 4,557 detached houses in Concord (66.4% of units) and 357 attached townhouses (5.2%). It also counts 1,515 units (22.1%) in buildings of five or more units. A detached house can usually take an outdoor condenser, but an apartment or condo may be limited by the building's rules, the available outdoor space or the electrical service.
## Small buildings in between

Between the detached houses and the large complexes sit 154 units in two-unit buildings and 280 in buildings of three or four units. Each has its own mix of owners, tenants and shared walls, and who may place an outdoor unit, or where, is worth settling before equipment is ordered. Newer construction counts too: 1,379 Concord units date from 2000 or later, and the age of a building says little about whether its layout leaves room for ducts.
## Central air, window units or ductless

Many older homes were built without central air, and some leave little room for large ducts. A ductless mini-split can cool a single room or a few rooms without ductwork, and a multi-head system can serve more of the house. It is not always the right answer, and a ducted system may suit some houses better.
- **Ducted central air:** works well where good ductwork already exists and has room for the airflow.
- **Ductless mini-split:** useful where ducts are missing, undersized or hard to reach.
- **Heat pump:** one system that both heats and cools, covered on the [heat pump page](/cities/concord/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
## Sizing is the decision that matters

Oversized air conditioners cool quickly but may cycle on and off, which can leave the air clammy and the compressor working harder. Undersized units run all afternoon and never catch up. We assess the home's load before quoting rather than relying on a rule of thumb.
## Repair calls

If the system stops cooling, a few checks come first: the thermostat, the breaker, a dirty filter or a frozen coil. Some of these you can check yourself, and some need a licensed technician. Call (508) 786-8755, and we will give you a free written estimate before any repair begins.

faq.q: Can I add air conditioning to a Concord house without ducts?
faq.a: Often yes. A ductless mini-split puts a small indoor head on a wall or ceiling and links it to the outdoor unit with a slim refrigerant line, so there are no ducts to run. One head serves a room and multi-head systems serve more. Layout and load decide whether it fits, and we assess both before quoting.

faq.q: Will my condo or apartment association allow an outdoor unit?
faq.a: That varies by building, so ask your association or landlord before you buy equipment. Concord has 1,515 units in buildings of five or more units (ACS 2022), and rules on outdoor equipment can differ from one building to the next.

faq.q: Is a Concord home built after 2000 easier to cool?
faq.a: Not automatically. The ACS 2022 counts 1,379 units built in 2000 or later, but ducts, insulation and sun exposure differ house to house. We size from the actual load and the layout rather than the build year.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Concord's electric utility is the Concord Municipal Light Plant, so the Mass Save heat pump rebate mainly reaches gas-heated homes. Oil heats 1,794 Concord homes, bottled gas 302 and electricity 583: those are the houses where a heat pump replaces the system outright.
body: ## Start with the utility

Because the Concord Municipal Light Plant is a municipal utility, Mass Save's heat pump rebate mainly reaches gas-heated homes. Oil, propane and electric houses usually turn to the light plant's own program, and we do not quote what it pays. Ask the light plant for current terms.
## The Mass Save headline

For homes that qualify, the 2026 whole-home rebate is $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500, and the house must be weatherized first. The full conditions sit on our [heat pump overview](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
## Which Concord houses change the most

The ACS 2022 counts 1,794 oil-heated homes (27.9%), 583 on electricity (9.1%) and 302 on bottled gas (4.7%). In those homes a heat pump would stand in for the fuel now burned or the resistance now used. Gas, at 3,545 homes, is the largest group, and for those the question is whether to add a heat pump beside the boiler or furnace instead of replacing it.
## Age against the weatherization test

Concord has 4,497 units built before 1980 (65.5%) and 1,379 built in 2000 or later (20.1%), of which 618 date from 2010 on. The newer units clear the age part of the weatherization test on their own. For the older ones, a Home Energy Assessment is the step that tells you how much sealing and insulation work stands in the way.
## Detached houses and apartment buildings

The ACS counts 4,557 detached houses (66.4%) and 1,515 units in buildings of five or more (22.1%). A detached house has room for an outdoor unit and can often take a multi-head ductless system. In an apartment building, the outdoor space and the electrical service may be shared, so the building comes into the decision.
## Sizing first

A house worth a median $1,018,100 deserves a system sized to its numbers. We assess the heating load before we quote, because a unit that is too small can leave rooms cold in January. For the cooling side, see our [air conditioning page](/cities/concord/air-conditioning-installation-repair).

faq.q: Which rebate applies to my Concord house?
faq.a: It depends on the fuel. In a municipal territory like Concord, the Mass Save route mainly serves gas-heated homes, while oil, propane and electric houses usually look to the light plant's own program. Check with the Concord Municipal Light Plant and masssave.com before ordering.

faq.q: Does my 1960s Concord house need weatherizing before a heat pump?
faq.a: For the Mass Save whole-home rebate, a house built before 2000 needs either a Home Energy Assessment recommending under $1,000 of work or completed recommendations. Concord has 1,721 units from 1960 to 1979, so for many an assessment is the first step.

faq.q: Can a ductless mini-split replace my whole heating system?
faq.a: Sometimes. A multi-head system can carry a whole house if the load is modest and the layout suits it. In other houses a mini-split covers part of the home and the old system stays as backup. A load assessment decides which case applies.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Oil heats more than a quarter of Concord's occupied homes, and oil systems need an annual cleaning and tune-up. Owners occupy 75.5% of households, and renters the rest, so the landlord or the owner usually decides when service happens.
body: ## The yearly checkup, by fuel

Oil equipment wants cleaning every year, and fuel oil heats 1,794 occupied Concord homes, a bit over a quarter. Gas heats 3,545, the largest group, and a gas boiler or furnace benefits from an annual look at its burner, venting and safety controls. Electricity heats 583 homes and bottled gas 302. Heat pumps ask less: clean filters and a clear outdoor unit.
## What a visit can cover
- Burner and combustion readings, where the system burns fuel.
- Filter, blower and coil inspection.
- Flue and venting inspection, a safety item.
- Thermostat and control checks.
- Condensate drain and outdoor unit checks on cooling equipment.
## Owners and renters

Concord has 4,863 owner-occupied households (75.5%), where the owner chooses when service happens. The 1,576 renter households depend on a landlord to book it. A visit before the cold weather arrives is cheap protection for either group.
## The calendar
Heating service fits late summer or early fall, ahead of mid-September when the heating season begins. Cooling service fits spring. Call (508) 786-8755 to schedule.
## Older equipment, older houses

The median Concord home dates to 1967, and 1,498 units go back to 1939 or earlier. Equipment in houses of that age is worth a closer look at the heat exchanger, the pipework and the venting, since a defect there can turn a routine visit into a replacement conversation. If it does, the estimate is written and free before work starts.
## Why the schedule matters for a big oil group

Concord ranks 32nd of 50 towns for oil heat, so the town sits below the middle, yet 1,794 homes still depend on it. Each of them has a burner nozzle, a filter and a combustion chamber that drift out of adjustment as the months pass. An unserviced oil unit tends to announce itself on the coldest night, which is the worst time to find a worn part, so spring and late summer are better dates for the work.
## Vacant houses
With 424 vacant units in the ACS count, some Concord equipment sits idle for long stretches. A system that has not run for a season is worth a start-up check before the weather turns.

faq.q: What does yearly oil boiler service involve for a Concord home?
faq.a: Once a year. Soot can build up in the combustion area and affect reliability, so book the cleaning before the heating season starts in mid-September. If the boiler is old, ask the technician to note worn parts so you can plan ahead.

faq.q: Is a tune-up worth it on a newer system?
faq.a: Generally yes. Newer equipment still collects dust, and filters, drains and controls still need attention. A yearly visit catches a small problem before it turns into a breakdown.

faq.q: Should I service a Concord furnace in a house that sat empty?
faq.a: A start-up check is sensible. The ACS 2022 counts 424 vacant units in town, and equipment that did not run for a season can hide wear, leaks or a dead control until the first cold night.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Concord's housing spans old and new: 14.4% of units date from 1980 to 1999 and 9.0% from 2010 or later. Tighter modern houses and older leaky ones can have different air problems.
body: ## Older houses and newer ones breathe differently

The ACS 2022 splits Concord's 6,863 units into age bands: 1,379 date from 2000 or later and 618 of those from 2010 or later (9.0%), while 987 (14.4%) date from 1980 to 1999. Newer houses are usually built tighter, which saves energy but lets moisture, cooking fumes and furnishing chemicals linger unless ventilation moves them out. Older houses leak more air, which can dilute some pollutants and also draws in dust, pollen and damp basement air.
## The oldest part of the housing stock

Homes from 1939 or earlier number 1,498, and 1,278 more date from 1940 to 1959. Basements, plaster and old framing in buildings of that vintage respond to moisture swings, so humidity control protects the structure as well as the people living in it. A sealed-up basement and a damp one are different problems, and a visit can tell which one a house has.
## The usual suspects
- **Filters:** a clean filter of a suitable grade cuts the dust moving through ducts.
- **Humidity:** winter air runs dry and summer air runs damp, and a comfortable middle range suits both people and woodwork.
- **Ventilation:** kitchen and bathroom fans should vent outdoors, and tight houses may need a planned source of fresh air.
- **Ductwork:** dust and debris collect over the years, and leaky ducts can pull from attics and basements.
- **Combustion safety:** fuel-burning equipment needs proper venting, and a carbon monoxide alarm is cheap insurance.
## Fuel-burning equipment and air
Gas heats 3,545 occupied Concord homes and oil heats 1,794. Equipment on either fuel puts combustion products up the flue, so a cracked liner or a blocked vent matters more than any filter upgrade.
## Closed-up houses and duct cleaning

The ACS counts 424 vacant Concord units. A house shut up for months can hold stale, humid air, and airing it out helps before anyone moves in. Duct cleaning is only sometimes useful, for instance after renovation, and an inspection shows whether it would help.
## Where it connects

Upgraded filters, humidifiers, dehumidifiers and ventilators work with the heating and cooling system, so an undersized system can undercut them. The [Concord page](/cities/concord) has the local numbers. To book an assessment, call (508) 786-8755.

faq.q: Is my newer Concord house too tight for good air quality?
faq.a: Not necessarily, but tighter houses depend on ventilation to carry out moisture and indoor pollutants. Check that kitchen and bathroom fans vent outside and work well, and ask whether a ventilator would help.
Not always. It can help after renovation work or visible contamination, but routine cleaning is not necessary in every house. Filter changes and a basic inspection usually come first.

faq.q: Can a vacant Concord house have air quality problems?
faq.a: It can. A house closed up for months may hold stale or humid air, and musty smells are a reason to look for moisture. Opening it up and checking the system before occupancy is a sensible first step.
